To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the spontaneous data set outperforms the acted data set in the recognition of vocal emotion; 2) the unweighted vote method outperforms the stacked generalisation method in the recognition of emotional speech; 3) the stacked generalisation and the unweighted vote methods are superior to the traditional classification methods.

(i) the best classification performance is achieved by the combination of a support vector machine and a decision tree classifier, (ii) the combination of a Gaussian mixture model classifier and a support vector machine classifier is the best performing single classification technique, and (iii) the combination of Gaussian mixture model and decision tree classifiers performs better than a combination of Gaussian mixture and support vector machines, but worse than the combination of a decision tree and a support vector machines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic recognition of emotion in speech.
the automatic classification of emotion from the speech signal and the application of this to call centre systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a combination of the two data sources (acted and natural) and the use of a combined classification method (stacked generalisation) can yield a significant improvement over a traditional single data source and single classification method.
this thesis has successfully demonstrated that the use of a combination of classifiers can be used to increase the performance of spoken emotion recognition systems.
the use of acted emotional speech is not a viable alternative to natural, spontaneous emotional data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to improve the accuracy of spoken emotion recognition in a call-centre context.
we have shown that the two data sources, acted and spontaneous speech, are both suitable sources for the application of emotion recognition.
we have shown that there is a difference between the two data sets and that we can improve on existing methods of classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of training data source is important and that the use of ensemble classification methods can improve the accuracy of emotion recognition.
the best performance is achieved by combining the best performing individual classifiers.
